topStories.headline: 'Dutton Ranch,' the Yellowstone Spinoff Filmed in Ferris, Renewed for Season 2
topStories.dek: The Paramount+ series starring Kelly Reilly and Cole Hauser — shot primarily on a 5,200-acre Ferris property — was renewed before its nine-episode first season finished airing in July.
topStories.body:
Ferris had its national close-up over the past year as the primary filming location for 'Dutton Ranch,' the Yellowstone spinoff that premiered May 15 on Paramount+ and the Paramount Network. The series stars Kelly Reilly and Cole Hauser reprising their roles as Beth Dutton and Rip Wheeler, and filmed in and around Ferris from August 2025 through March 2026, according to D Magazine and WFAA. Additional scenes were shot in Boyd, Weatherford, Cleburne, and other North Texas locations to build out the fictional South Texas town of Rio Paloma.

A 5,200-acre Ferris property — formerly owned by Trinity Industries CEO W. Ray Wallace — served as the rival ranch owner's home base in the show, according to D Magazine. The nine-episode first season concluded in July 2026. Paramount+ renewed the show for a second season before it finished airing, with Benjamin Cavell set to serve as showrunner after Chad Feehan's departure before the premiere, per Yahoo Entertainment.

The show's roots in Ferris trace to August 2025, when the city announced it had been selected as a primary filming location under the working title 'Rio Palo.' City Manager Brooks Williams said at the time: 'This is a proud and fun moment for Ferris. Ferris helped build Texas and the nation. Ferris bricks are in streets, schools, and courthouses across this country. This city has evolved, adapted, and grown. Paramount's decision to film here is one more chapter in that story.' The quote appeared in the city's official press release, republished by In The Know Ellis.

The production was coordinated by King Street Productions and 101 Studios. Executive producer David Glasser told D Magazine that the decision to shoot entirely on location — rather than using green screens — was central to making the show feel authentically Texan.

topStories.headline: Chipotle Coming to 391 N. Sonoma Trail in Ennis Later This Month
topStories.dek: A DFW-wide expansion announced October 5 includes a new Ennis location converting a former restaurant on N. Sonoma Trail, with a state licensing completion date of October 30.
topStories.body:
Ennis is set to get a new Chipotle Mexican Grill at 391 N. Sonoma Trail, with an opening expected later in October. CW33/KDAF reported on October 5 that Chipotle Mexican Grill is opening five new locations across the Dallas-Fort Worth area by year's end. The expansion includes new restaurants in Dallas, Ennis, Lewisville, and Corsicana. The opening schedule began with a Dallas location on October 6, followed by the Ennis location at 391 N. Sonoma Trail later this month.

A Texas Department of Licensing and Regulation filing (project TABS2026012174) confirms the construction details. The TDLR record lists a start date of May 13, 2026, a completion date of October 30, 2026, and an estimated construction cost of $1,000,000. The scope of work is the conversion of an existing freestanding restaurant — 2,949 square feet — into a new Chipotle Mexican Grill with a pick-up window, including demolition, interior build-out, and new mechanical, electrical, and plumbing systems.

Four of the five new DFW-area locations in this expansion round will feature a Chipotlane drive-through pickup lane designed for digital orders, according to CW33. The Zabalist construction tracker, which aggregates Texas TDLR records, lists the Ennis Chipotle among five projects in the city expected to complete within the next 120 days, representing part of roughly $30.4 million in active Ennis construction registered over the past 12 months.

topStories.headline: Early Voting Opens October 19 in Ellis County Ahead of November 3 General Election
topStories.dek: Ellis County's gubernatorial general and special elections are less than four weeks away, with early voting running October 19–30 and Election Day set for Tuesday, November 3.
topStories.body:
Ellis County residents will head to the polls for a general and special election on Tuesday, November 3, 2026. Early voting runs October 19 through October 30, according to the Ellis County Elections Department. Sample ballots and polling location information are available at elliscountytx.gov. As of October 1, the county had 159,039 registered voters on the rolls.

The voter registration deadline for this election has passed — October 5 was the last day to register or make changes to a voter record. However, October 23 is the last day for the Elections office to receive a mail ballot application. Voters can call the Elections Department at 972-825-5195 ext. 2 for precinct and sample ballot assistance.

The 2026 cycle is a gubernatorial general election year in Texas, meaning statewide races appear on the ballot alongside county-level contests. Ellis County administers elections for 63 political subdivisions, including 20 cities, 11 school districts, 6 water districts, 14 municipal utility districts, and 12 emergency service districts, according to the county's Elections page. The county Elections Department posted sample ballots by precinct on its website in September.

events.title: Stars of Texas Festival — Aaron Watson, Brad Paisley, Travis Tritt
events.description: Three-night country music festival at the Historic Texas Motorplex featuring Aaron Watson on Friday, Brad Paisley on Saturday, and Travis Tritt on Sunday, plus drag racing, bull riding, BBQ, a kids zone, and lantern releases each night. Single-day and weekend passes available.

moreNews.headline: Ennis ISD Students Off Friday and Monday for Staff Development Day and District Holiday
moreNews.body: Ennis ISD students have no school on Friday, October 9 (Staff Development Day) and Monday, October 12 (District Holiday), per the district's approved 2026–2027 calendar. The first grading period ended Thursday, October 8; the second grading period begins Tuesday, October 13. The district website also notes that breakfast and lunch are free for all EISD students this school year through the federal Community Eligibility Program.

moreNews.headline: Ennis Marching Band Earns Back-to-Back First Division Superior at Mesquite Festival
moreNews.body: The Ennis High School Marching Band earned a First Division Superior rating for the second consecutive year at the Mesquite Marching Festival, held at Mesquite Memorial Stadium, according to the Ennis Daily News (October 3, 2026). The E-Band has a long tradition of superior ratings at regional marching competitions going back decades.

moreNews.headline: Ellis County Countywide Burn Ban Remains in Effect
moreNews.body: The Ellis County Commissioners' Court voted to issue a countywide burn ban at its July 21, 2026, meeting, and the ban remains in effect as of this week per the county's official news flash page. The ban applies to all unincorporated areas of Ellis County. Residents can check elliscountytx.gov for any updates to the order.

moreNews.headline: Ennis City Commission Holds Special Meeting October 9
moreNews.body: The Ennis City Commission convened a special meeting this morning, October 9, 2026, at 10:00 AM, according to a notice posted on the city's official events calendar. A 211-KB agenda PDF was posted to ennistx.gov ahead of the meeting. Agenda items were not described in the calendar listing; the full agenda is available at ennistx.gov.
